slides.title: Metallic taste. Then a seizure. Then the rhythm goes.
slides.sub: Local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST): recognition to lipid emulsion.

slides.pearl: It can skip the CNS signs, or show up late.

slides.body: Get the LAST kit and lipid emulsion. Tell the team out loud what you suspect.
Hypoxia and acidosis make toxicity worse. Ventilate well. Treat seizures with a benzodiazepine.
Give 20% lipid emulsion at the first sign of serious toxicity. Follow the ASRA LAST checklist.

bullets: Start ACLS with smaller epinephrine doses
Avoid vasopressin, calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers
Do not treat arrhythmias with more local anesthetic
Alert the team for possible bypass/ECMO

slides.title: Lipid lives where blocks happen.
slides.body: Know where your LAST kit is before your next block.

caption:
Ringing ears and a metallic taste right after the block. Would you call LAST before the seizure? 🧠

Swipe for the response: stop injecting and call for help → airway and 100% O2, benzodiazepine for seizures → 20% lipid emulsion early, per the ASRA LAST checklist → modified ACLS if the heart stops.

💡 LAST can present atypically: late, or with cardiac signs and no warning symptoms.
